note: Outside on four of five, and the one match is real: he has trained since high school, calls exercise a hobby, tracks his calories and has taken his body fat from 25% to about 20% on his own — nothing like the deconditioned, gym-averse profile the ICP excludes. Everything else fails. Successful: a radiology student in a new job following a military medical discharge. Income: about $100 a month spare, no savings, a loan being taken for tuition and $13,000-$14,000 of arrears just cleared. Neglected health: his health is not neglected, it is a treated chronic condition — a herniated disc under a doctor's care that stops him sitting through a class. Good to great: this is pain relief, in his own words, 'living with pain is not life'. The wider point for the rollup is that this is the most motivated prospect in the batch by a distance, gave a 100% commitment before hearing the price, and could not buy at any structure offered — while two prospects who fit the stated ICP almost perfectly declined on value. On this batch the ICP's income criterion is doing the only real work, and it is filtering on cash position rather than on anything about the person.
